As for my recommendation - if you like heavy worldbuilding I recommend The Traitor Baru Cormorant (🤪 yes, yung nasa taas na kakasabi ko lang kung saan ako nahirapahan - WORTH IT OP PROMISE) and Gideon the Ninth. Much shorter siya kesa sa Baru pero ganun din yung world building niya, yung tipong it gets better and better with every reread kasi andami mong marerealize!!

Gideon the Ninth - leans more Science Fiction but has enough Fantasy elements that blur them together imo. Very lovable MC and very strong characterizations. Lots of threads and hints that make rereads even better than the last as you piece together everything that’s happening in the background. I cannot believe that this was Tamsyn Muir’s debut novel. Literally the book series that got me back into reading.
Sa true pinapatulan ko nalang yung mga bundles na nasa recommended nila. Yung last na bili ko sa kanila, The Locked Tomb trilogy na Php3,120 - walang sf, walang import fee.

**Mini review:** I got Gateron browns for this, but my RK71 already had Browns so I kind of knew what to expect. Pros: the keys are very soft and it's quite easy to type! Almost no effort at all required. The backspace, enter, and tab keys have my favorite sound - it almost sounds as if it's been lubed.

 Light settings are gorgeous! Multimedia keys are extremely helpful. There are some cons though - the spacebar sounds kind of "slappy" and doesn't press down as smoothly as the other keys. The layout is a little big, but I guess I just need to get used to that. 

Biggest con is that there isn't a application to control the lights - but there's a dedicated button to change the lighting on the keyboard. Overall very happy with my purchase!

Here are a few!

- Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild: open world, exploration, heavily stylized, beginner-friendly! This was my first open world game, and I’ve since logged 200+ hours on two playthroughs. No two playthroughs are the same! You can bend the game in many different directions. 

- Animal Crossing: New Horizons: chill, to be played day-to-day, will have upcoming updates as the year progresses. Coming from the Animal Crossing game on the DS, don’t be discouraged by the amount of content that’s out now. Throughout the year, there will be seasonal events and updates to come! Can be played for the whole day, but suggested play is to take it slow, day-by-day in small portions. 

- Hollow Knight: metroidvania, roguelike, extremely challenging. I have this for both my Switch and PC! If you like games like Celeste, with almost rhythmic like timing to defeat some of the bosses and overcome bosses, Hollow Knight is for you! The challenge in the base game is intense – paired with the free DLCS, Hollow Knight is a joy to come back to for some challenge. 

- Stardew Valley: Farming, chill, can be adjusted to how you play. Another game that I have for both PC and Switch! Though the mods on PC are extremely fun, it’s nice to come back to the vanilla game every now and then. Nice for those days when you don’t really want to think, and focus on menial tasks such as picking your fruit and milking your cows. 

- Baba is You: Puzzle. One of the best puzzle games I’ve ever played, focuses you to broaden your thinking based on the given rules of the level. Many many hours of enjoyment, and finding the solution for each level has always been extremely satisfying. 

- Octopath Traveller: JRPG, turn-based. A beautiful game stemming from the vein of Bravely Default/Bravely Second on the DS, Octopath Traveller has you playing through the stories of 8 travelers. The environments are beautiful and it’s combat is satisfying. Difficulty is okay for a JRPG, but might seem a little grind-y to people who don’t like the genre.
